title: Pocket Checklist
pin_title: ADHD Pocket Checklist: Keep a Tiny List on Paper So You Don't Forget Keys and Wallet
description: Forgetting keys or a wallet happens when your hands are full and your brain is already moving. Write a short checklist on a small card and keep it in your pocket or bag. Glance at it while you lock the door. Checking one card takes seconds and replaces the scramble later. A paper list you can touch works even when your phone is buried. #ADHD #ADHDChecklist #Forgetfulness #ADHDTips

title: Soft Landing
pin_title: ADHD Soft Landing After Work: One Calm Ritual So Your Evening Starts Gently
description: Walking in the door with a full brain can make the rest of the day feel heavy. Choose one soft landing: hang your bag, drink a glass of water, or sit for two minutes. Do only that before anything else. A tiny ritual tells your body the work day is finished and the evening can begin without pressure. It is a kindness to yourself. #ADHD #EveningRoutine #SelfCare #ADHDTips
scene_prompt: {mascot} standing in a cozy entryway next to a hanging bag and a glass of water on a small wooden shelf, soft warm light from a nearby lamp, a leafy plant in the background, everything fully visible and brightly lit

title: One Drawer Only
pin_title: ADHD One Drawer Rule: Empty Just One Drawer Today So Clutter Feels Possible
description: A whole room of clutter can freeze you. Pick one single drawer and empty it onto the floor. Sort into keep, trash, and later in ten minutes. Put the keep items back. One finished drawer is a real win you can see. Tomorrow you can choose another if you want. Progress is still progress when the rest of the room waits. #ADHD #Organization #Clutter #ADHDTips

title: Water First
pin_title: ADHD Water First: Drink One Glass Before Coffee So Your Morning Starts Kindly
description: Morning fog makes it easy to skip water. Put a glass by the sink the night before and drink it before you touch the coffee maker. The cold water is a small signal that the day has started. Your body gets what it needs and your brain gets a gentle wake-up. One glass is enough to count as done. #ADHD #Hydration #MorningRoutine #ADHDTips

title: Five Minute Floor
pin_title: ADHD Five Minute Floor: Clear a Small Patch of Floor So Walking Feels Easier
description: Tripping over things adds friction to every trip across the room. Set a five-minute timer and clear only the path from the door to the chair. Put items in a box for later. A clear strip of floor makes the room feel lighter and moving feels safer. You do not have to finish the whole space. #ADHD #Organization #SmallWins #ADHDTips

title: Kind Note to Self
pin_title: ADHD Kind Note to Self: Leave a Gentle Reminder Where You Will See It Tomorrow
description: Hard days make self-talk sharp. Write one kind sentence on a sticky note and place it where tomorrow-you will find it, like the fridge or the desk. Something simple like you did enough today. Reading it later is a soft restart. The note is a gift from past-you to future-you. #ADHD #SelfCompassion #ADHDTips #Kindness

title: Visible Water
pin_title: ADHD Visible Water: Keep Your Bottle in Sight So You Actually Drink It
description: A water bottle in a cupboard is easy to forget. Leave it on the desk or the table where your eyes land often. When you notice it, take a sip. Seeing the bottle is the reminder. No app or alarm needed. A bottle you can see is a quiet friend that asks for nothing. #ADHD #Hydration #ADHDTips #HealthyHabits

title: Shoes With Keys
pin_title: ADHD Shoes With Keys: Pair Them So Leaving the House Takes One Motion
description: Hunting for keys when you are already late adds stress. Put your keys inside one shoe or on top of both shoes by the door. When you put the shoes on, the keys are already in your hand. One motion instead of two searches. The pair lives by the door so future-you finds them together. #ADHD #Forgetfulness #ADHDTips #LeavingTheHouse
